definition.interpretation: The experiment yielded an accuracy of 0.86 for the adaptive policy model under conditions simulating rigid vs adaptive decision-making latency, exceeding the 0.8 threshold set by the hypothesis. This suggests that adaptive policies maintain higher functional performance in scenarios where rigid subordination might otherwise cause plan delays.
definition.limitations: The simulation uses abstracted success rates (0.65 for rigid, 0.85 for adaptive) rather than modeling specific cognitive architecture dynamics. Result interpretability is restricted to the relationship between decision flexibility and throughput.
definition.next_step: Refine the hypothesis to specifically measure the delta in error rates under variable latency thresholds rather than a binary rigidity condition.

definition.cost: Computational validation of refined latency thresholds and replication of success rates across broader random seed ranges.
definition.next_experiment: Replicate experiment with refined parameters focusing on latency thresholds.
definition.reason: Initial experiment supports the hypothesis but relies on simplified parameters; further refinement is necessary to establish the mechanism of failure.
definition.stop_condition: Failure to demonstrate consistent performance degradation in rigid policy configurations at varied latency intervals.
definition.uncertainty: The mechanism driving the performance gap remains an assumption of the model; identifying the structural point of failure requires more granular latency testing.

proposal.summary: Interpreting experiment results on rigid versus adaptive obedience policies and determining the next phase of research within the obedience_limits topic.
proposal.title: Research Update: Obedience Latency and Cognitive Constraints
